definition: A crossing of fibers from one side of the neuraxis to the other. The main decussations are the pyramidal (corticospinal, cervicomedullary junction), the sensory (medial lemniscus, lower medulla), the spinothalamic (anterior white commissure, within the cord), the optic chiasm and the superior cerebellar peduncle (midbrain). Where a pathway crosses determines whether a lesion produces ipsilateral or contralateral signs.
